title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE DARK HOUSE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Trevor Banks, a railroad track inspector from Omaha, Nebraska.
Last spring, he moved into his late grandpa's little house on Larkspur Court.
Then December came, and he found out Larkspur Court takes Christmas lights very, very seriously.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BLACK HOLE
segments.quote: It is far better to light the candle than to curse the darkness.
segments.author: William L. Watkinson
lines: Every house on the street glowed. Except his.
His neighbor Gordy, eleven-time winner of the street's lights trophy, called it the black hole of Larkspur Court.
Trevor grumbled about it to Hattie, seventy-nine, from across the street. She quoted an old English preacher, William Watkinson:
It is far better to light the candle than to curse the darkness.
So Trevor stopped grumbling and drove to the hardware store.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LADDER
segments.quote: Act as if it were impossible to fail.
segments.author: Dorothea Brande
lines: He had never hung a single light. The ladder wobbled. So did his knees.
Then he remembered his mom's favorite line, from the writer Dorothea Brande:
Act as if it were impossible to fail.
So he climbed like a man who knew what he was doing. By Friday, his roof was glowing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE MOOSE
segments.quote: Whenever a friend succeeds, a little something in me dies.
segments.author: Gore Vidal
lines: The next morning, Gordy added a twenty-foot moose that sings.
Trevor felt sour, and he knew it. The writer Gore Vidal once joked:
Whenever a friend succeeds, a little something in me dies.
Trevor laughed at himself. Then he bought six thousand more lights anyway.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BLACKOUT
segments.quote: A man who never makes a mistake will never make anything.
segments.author: Edward John Phelps
lines: He plugged it all in. Pop. Every house on the street went dark.
Gordy's moose sank to the lawn with a long, sad groan.
Hattie brought him cocoa and an old line from the American diplomat Edward John Phelps:
A man who never makes a mistake will never make anything.
So Trevor took down half the lights, added timers, and his house looked better than ever.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE ICE STORM
segments.quote: The friends of my adversity I shall always cherish most.
segments.author: Ulysses S. Grant
lines: The night before judging, an ice storm tore down Gordy's lights. And Gordy had a bad back.
Trevor could finally win. But a plaque at the rail yard held words from Ulysses S. Grant:
The friends of my adversity I shall always cherish most.
Meaning, the friends who show up in your hard times. So at six a.m., Trevor was on Gordy's roof.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: CONTEST NIGHT
segments.quote: Blessed is the season which engages the whole world in a conspiracy of love.
segments.author: Hamilton Wright Mabie
lines: Only one house was still dark: Hattie's. Her late husband Leon always did the lights.
In Leon's box, an old card held words from the writer Hamilton Wright Mabie:
Blessed is the season which engages the whole world in a conspiracy of love.
So Trevor and Gordy lit Hattie's house together. She won. The moose sang. Off key.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Light a candle. Climb anyway. Laugh at yourself. Learn. Show up. Share the light.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Light a candle. Climb anyway. Laugh at yourself. Learn. Show up. Share the light.
I strung Christmas lights once myself. My cat wore them until February.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
